witnesses.name: Leningrad Codex
witnesses.institution: National Library of Russia, St. Petersburg (Firkovich Collection B 19 A)
witnesses.terms: Public-domain manuscript (dated 1008/9 AD); reproduction terms depend on the specific facsimile host and were not independently confirmed as embeddable.
witnesses.note: The base text of the Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC) transcription used for data/bible/hebrew.

witnesses.name: Aleppo Codex
witnesses.institution: Israel Museum, Jerusalem (Shrine of the Book)
witnesses.note: Approximately 40% of the codex (essentially the whole Torah, Gen.1.1-Deu.28.16) has been missing since 1947-48; a few other leaves (part of the opening of Song of Songs, etc.) are also lost.

witnesses.name: Cairo Genizah fragments
witnesses.date: c. 870 AD - 19th c. AD (deposits span many centuries)
witnesses.institution: Ben Ezra Synagogue, Fustat (Old Cairo); fragments now chiefly at Cambridge University Library (Taylor-Schechter Collection) and other libraries
witnesses.note: Not a single manuscript: a store of c. 300,000+ fragments (biblical, liturgical, documentary) accumulated from the 9th to 19th centuries; includes some of the oldest dated biblical codex fragments (Cairo Codex of the Prophets tradition) and early Masoretic witnesses. `contents` is left empty (too heterogeneous to give as verse ranges) and it is excluded from coverage-summary.json accordingly.

witnesses.name: Samaritan Pentateuch (representative MSS; Abisha Scroll)
witnesses.date: oldest extant MSS c. 12th-14th c. AD (the Abisha Scroll's core is traditionally claimed far earlier by the Samaritan community; independent codicological dating is much later); the SP as a textual tradition is ancient (attested distinctively by the 2nd century BC, e.g. in proto-Samaritan Qumran texts)
witnesses.institution: Samaritan community, Mount Gerizim/Nablus (Abisha Scroll kept by the Samaritan high priest); other SP MSS in the British Library, Cambridge UL, John Rylands Library
witnesses.note: Covers only the five books of the Torah (the sole canon of the Samaritans). The Abisha Scroll's own great age is a traditional Samaritan claim, not an independently verified codicological date; other Samaritan Pentateuch MSS are more securely dated to the medieval period. Textual affinities with 'proto-Samaritan' Qumran manuscripts (e.g. 4QpaleoExodm) show the tradition itself long predates any surviving copy.

witnesses.name: Great Isaiah Scroll
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: The only complete biblical scroll from Qumran; virtually the entire Book of Isaiah is preserved intact on 17 sheets.

witnesses.name: Isaiah Scroll b
witnesses.date: 1st c. BC - 1st c. AD (c. 50 BC-50 AD)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Substantial but incomplete; closer to the Masoretic consonantal text than 1QIsaa. Several columns are lost or fragmentary.

witnesses.name: Isaiah Scroll (4Q56)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary; one of ~21 Isaiah manuscripts found at Qumran.

witnesses.name: paleo-Hebrew Exodus (4Q22)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Written in the archaic paleo-Hebrew script; closely related to the Samaritan Pentateuch's textual tradition (minus its sectarian expansions).

witnesses.name: paleo-Hebrew Deuteronomy (4Q45)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Written in the paleo-Hebrew script.

witnesses.name: Numbers b (4Q27)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Extensive Numbers manuscript with a text-form closer to the Samaritan tradition and LXX than to the Masoretic Text in places.

witnesses.name: Deuteronomy q (4Q44)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Preserves the Song of Moses (Deut 32) in a text-form close to that presupposed by the Septuagint.

witnesses.name: Samuel b (4Q52)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: One of the very oldest Qumran biblical manuscripts (3rd century BC).

witnesses.name: Samuel a (4Q51)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: The most extensive Samuel manuscript from Qumran; often agrees with the Septuagint's Vorlage against the (shorter) Masoretic Text, e.g. at 1 Samuel 11.

witnesses.name: Kings (4Q54)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Small fragment of 1 Kings.

witnesses.name: Jeremiah a (4Q70)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Close to the Masoretic Text's (longer) edition of Jeremiah.

witnesses.name: Jeremiah b (4Q71)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Reflects the shorter Hebrew edition of Jeremiah that underlies the Septuagint, roughly 1/8 shorter than the Masoretic Text.

witnesses.name: Ezekiel a (4Q73)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary.

witnesses.name: Daniel a (1Q71)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary; one of the earliest Daniel manuscripts, close in time to the book's composition.

witnesses.name: Daniel c (4Q114)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Paleographically among the very oldest copies of Daniel, within decades of the book's composition.

witnesses.name: Minor Prophets scroll (Wadi Murabba'at)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: From Wadi Murabba'at (Bar Kokhba period), not Qumran proper; a nearly complete Book of the Twelve very close to the Masoretic consonantal text, showing the MT tradition's stability by the early 2nd century AD.

witnesses.name: Minor Prophets c (4Q78)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary Book of the Twelve manuscript.

witnesses.name: Great Psalms Scroll (11Q5)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Covers roughly the last third of the Psalter but in a different order from the Masoretic Text and with additional compositions (e.g. Psalm 151, Sirach 51, 'Apostrophe to Zion'); its status (an alternate edition vs. a liturgical collection) is debated.

witnesses.name: Ecclesiastes a (4Q109)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: One of the earliest surviving copies of any Hebrew Bible book by absolute date, and important evidence for how early Ecclesiastes' final form existed.

witnesses.name: Song of Songs b (4Q107)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Preserves a shorter text-form of Song of Songs, missing verses found in the Masoretic Text.

witnesses.name: Ruth a (2Q16)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary.

witnesses.name: Lamentations a (5Q6)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary.

witnesses.name: Genesis b (4Q1)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary, non-contiguous.

witnesses.name: Leviticus b (4Q24)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Fragmentary.

witnesses.name: Judges a (4Q49)
witnesses.institution: Dead Sea Scrolls; Israel Antiquities Authority (Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, unless otherwise excavated/housed)
witnesses.note: Small fragment; may lack the section of Judges 6 found in later texts, of interest for the book's growth.

witnesses.name: Codex Vaticanus
witnesses.institution: Vatican Apostolic Library (Vat. gr. 1209)
witnesses.note: Original 4th-century hand lacks Gen.1.1-46.28 (supplied by a 15th-century restorer) and Psalm 106-138 (English numbering; a quire is missing); order and chapter/verse boundaries follow the Septuagint, only approximately mapped here onto the 39-book Hebrew-canon versification used elsewhere in this dataset.

witnesses.name: Codex Sinaiticus
witnesses.institution: Split between the British Library (London), Leipzig University Library, National Library of Russia, and Saint Catherine's Monastery (Sinai)
witnesses.note: Almost the entire Torah and Former Prophets (Genesis-2 Kings, and most of 1 Chronicles) are lost from the surviving OT portion; extant text effectively begins mid-1-Chronicles. Coverage given here is approximate at the whole-book level for the remaining books (Ezra onward), which themselves have further internal gaps not tracked individually.
